# Interim Phase 2 PK/PD Data Supports Weekly and Monthly Dosing in Obesity

**TALDEFGROBEP**

## % Myostatin Suppression at Week 12 in Overweight/Obese Adults

<visual_element id="e1">

Bar chart showing percentage of myostatin suppression from baseline at Week 12 in overweight/obese adults.

- **Y-axis:** % Myostatin Suppression From Baseline (0–100%), with increments of 20.
- **X-axis:** Dosing regimen.
- **100 mg Q1W:** 99% myostatin suppression (light blue bar).
- **150 mg Q4W:** 79% myostatin suppression (dark teal bar).

The 100 mg Q1W regimen shows 99% suppression, compared with 79% for the 150 mg Q4W regimen.

</visual_element>

## Taldefgrobep-Myostatin Complex at Week 12 in Overweight/Obese Adults

<visual_element id="e2">

Bar/range chart showing T/M complex concentrations at Week 12 for two dosing regimens.

- **Y-axis:** T/M Complex (nM), ranging from 2 to 14, with increments of 2.
- **X-axis:** Dosing regimen.
- **100 mg Q1W (light blue):**
  - High Estimate: **12.88**
  - Low Estimate: **6.44**
- **150 mg Q4W (blue-gray):**
  - High Estimate: **9.48**
  - Low Estimate: **4.74**

A horizontal red dotted reference line is labeled **ActRII IC₅₀**, positioned at approximately 5 nM.

Both dosing regimens show T/M complex concentration estimates at or above the ActRII IC₅₀ target level, including the lower estimate for 150 mg Q4W (4.74 nM), which is close to the reference line.

</visual_element>

## AT WEEK 12:

- Observed mean taldefgrobep concentrations are consistent with model-predicted
- Robust suppression of free myostatin throughout Q1W and Q4W dosing intervals
- T/M complex concentrations comparable between dosing regimens and at/above target ActRII IC₅₀

## KEY POINT

Interim data suggest monthly dosing can achieve robust myostatin suppression and formation of T/M complex levels at/above targeted ActRII IC₅₀ levels.

EXG001-307 (SMA Type 1) for the treatment of SMA Type 1 constitutes our Core
Product candidate, while ongoing evaluation in SMA Type 2 and SMA Type 3 represents
additional clinical exploration of the same vector. EXG001-307 (SMA Type 1) received IND
approval from the NMPA for the treatment of SMA Type 1 in June 2022. As of the Latest
Practicable Date, we have completed the Phase I/II clinical trial of EXG001-307 (SMA Type
1) in China, in which a total of 13 patients with SMA Type 1 were treated across the low-
and high-dose cohorts. The high-dose cohort (1.5×1014 vg/kg) demonstrated the most
notable functional improvement, consistent with a dose-response relationship. All the
treated patients in this cohort who were able to participate in the evaluations through the
data cutoff period achieved head control (100%), approximately two-thirds attained the
ability to sit without support (66.7%), two patients were able to stand with support
(22.2%), and three patients were able to make stepping movements (33.3%). In addition,
patients achieved a mean improvement in CHOP-INTEND score of 33.5 from baseline,
numerically higher than the CHOP-INTEND score improvements reported for
Zolgensma® (approximately 21-24 points), Evrysdi® (approximately 20 points), and
Spinraza® (approximately 11 points), at comparable assessment windows. As of the Latest
Practicable Date, all surviving patients had completed the primary observation period
through 18 months of age, and long-term four-year safety monitoring is ongoing.
Mechanism of Action
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is caused by mutations in the SMN1 gene, resulting
in a deficiency of the survival motor neuron (SMN) protein and progressive skeletal
muscle atrophy that impairs movement, swallowing and respiration. SMA severity varies
by age of onset, with infantile-onset SMA Type 1 presenting at or shortly after birth with
severe weakness, respiratory involvement and early mortality.

Based on non-clinical and clinical data, Biohaven initiated a Phase 2 study of taldefgrobep in the management of obesity in the fourth quarter of 2025.
In May 2024, we announced preclinical data from a diet-induced obesity mouse model, which showed treatment with taldefgrobep alfa together with a glucagon-like peptide-1 ("GLP-1") agonist produced greater reductions in body weight and fat mass, and a larger increase in lean muscle mass, compared to treatment with GLP-1 alone (see figure below).

Image: TALFA.jpg

Based on non-clinical and clinical data, Biohaven initiated a Phase 2 study of taldefgrobep in the management of obesity in the fourth quarter of 2025. In March 2026, we announced that enrollment in the study was complete. The study is evaluating the ability of taldefgrobep to reduce fat mass and total body weight while increasing lean muscle mass. As originally designed, the study is a placebo-controlled study evaluating two dosing schedules of taldefgrobep versus placebo. Approximately 150 participants were randomized to receive taldefgrobep or matching placebo over a 24-week double-blind treatment period followed by an additional 24 weeks of OLE during which all participants will receive taldefgrobep. Key endpoints include the change in total body weight, lean mass, fat mass, and metabolic parameters, along with a comprehensive assessment of safety. See below for trial design.

Image: talfa.jpg

The study is being amended to include an assessment of taldefgrobep in combination with a GLP-1-based therapy. As a result of the amended study design, we now anticipate topline data from the monotherapy and combination therapy portions of the trial in the second half of 2027.

At the lowest tested dose (2 × 10^{10} vg/animal [1.3×10^{13} vg/kg]), median survival increased from 15 days in vehicle-treated controls to 23 days, representing a statistically significant extension (p < 0.0001). This survival benefit was accompanied by measurable improvements in body weight (Figure 3C) and neuromotor function, including enhanced righting reflex (Figure 3D) and locomotor activity (Figure 3E). At the highest dose (2 × 10^{11} vg/animal [1.3×10^{14} vg/kg]), EXG001-307 achieved a maximum survival of 501 days and a median survival of 373 days, compared with 15 days in vehicle-treated mice.
